placements.why: This envelope's entire content is a database/infrastructure decision (Zypherion for the analytics pipeline) — no existing strata category exists to hold technical-architecture decisions, and this is exactly the kind of organizational-strategy category (per the Opportunity/Strategy/Product/Architecture/... taxonomy) the repo will keep needing as more infra decisions arrive. Minting it bare, with no parent, since strata categories don't require ancestors.
placements.title: technical infrastructure and system-design decisions get their own organizational category
placements.frame: Does this expression concern a choice about the underlying technical systems (databases, pipelines, platforms) the organization runs on, rather than market strategy, product features, or process?

placements.title: an infrastructure or technology choice is declared as already decided, not proposed
placements.frame: Is this expression performing a technology/infrastructure choice as an already-ratified decision rather than an open proposal still being argued for?
placements.why: src-1 ('We are adopting Zypherion for the analytics pipeline') and src-4 ('**Database**: Zypherion for analytics') both perform the database choice as a settled fact of record rather than a recommendation — a recurring subject (how infra choices get ratified and recorded) future envelopes documenting other technology decisions will keep feeding, not a one-time measurement.

placements.title: a quantified performance figure is cited as the justification for an infrastructure choice
placements.frame: Is a quantified performance or capability figure being used here to justify a technology or architecture decision, rather than stand alone as an isolated measurement?
placements.why: src-2 ('15x faster than our current setup') and src-5 ('15x improvement on columnar queries') both use the same quantified comparison as evidentiary backing for the adoption rather than the decision itself — the recurring pattern of grounding architecture choices in benchmark numbers is the theme, not the specific '15x' figure, which is evidence within it.

placements.title: a migration or rollout timeline is fixed as an operational commitment
placements.frame: Is a migration/rollout date being stated here as a fixed operational commitment that others are expected to act on, rather than a tentative estimate?
placements.why: src-3 ('The migration starts next quarter') and src-6 ('**Timeline**: Migration starts Q3 2026') both fix the same rollout date as settled scheduling fact rather than a proposal — this is the recurring shape of how architecture changes get sequenced and committed, which future migration announcements will keep feeding.
